# ClientPilot

> ClientPilot (https://clientpilot.dev) turns a freelance developer's profile into ready-to-publish client acquisition content: LinkedIn posts, cold outreach emails, a Dev.to article, freelance platform profiles, portfolio page copy and elevator pitches. Made by Dizid (https://dizid.com), Marc de Ruijter.

## What it does
- You sign in with Google and give it your portfolio URL, GitHub profile or a pasted CV; it drafts your profile (skills, stack, projects, target market) for you to check.
- One generation produces six content types from that profile: 7 LinkedIn posts, 6 outreach templates (LinkedIn DMs and emails: cold to a funded startup, a CTO and an agency, warm to a former colleague, a message after engaging with someone's post, a reply to a freelance platform inquiry), a 600-900 word Dev.to case-study article, reusable platform profile text (short bio, full bio, skills, availability, rate wording for Toptal, Arc.dev, freelance.nl and similar platforms), portfolio /hire page copy (headline, services with price ranges, case studies, why hire me, process, call to action), and elevator pitches (30-second pitch, X bio, LinkedIn headline, email signature, GitHub README, one-liner).
- Target context: describe an ideal client (startup, agency, a niche, or paste the prospect's website) and the messaging, pain points and positioning are tailored to that client. Several targets can share one profile.
- Every piece is editable inline, copied with one click, and tracked as draft, used or replied. Pro and Lifetime users can regenerate any single piece with their own feedback.
- Content is generated with Anthropic's Claude.

## Pricing
- Free: 1 preview generation with all content types (edit and copy included; regenerating a piece is Pro).
- Pro: $9 per month. Unlimited generations, all content types, regenerate any piece with your feedback. Cancel anytime by emailing dev@dizid.com (access runs to the end of the billing period); refund on request within 7 days of purchase.
- Lifetime: $69 one-time payment. Everything in Pro, lifetime updates, priority support.

## Who it is for
- Freelance and indie developers who want a steady stream of client-facing content without writing it from scratch each week.
- Not an API or auto-poster yet: you copy the content and publish it yourself (LinkedIn and Dev.to publishing integrations are on the roadmap).

## Blog (guides for freelance developers)
- [Blog index](https://clientpilot.dev/blog): all guides, newest first
- [How to set your freelance developer rate (with 2026 data)](https://clientpilot.dev/blog/freelance-developer-rates): Arc, Upwork, Malt and US BLS figures with their limits; hourly vs day rate vs fixed price; floor-rate calculation incl. platform fees; raising your rate
- [Freelance platform fees for developers compared (2026)](https://clientpilot.dev/blog/freelance-platform-fees-compared): Upwork, Fiverr, Contra, Malt, Toptal, Arc, Freelancer.com, PeoplePerHour, Braintrust, Lemon.io; free channels; a 30-day plan
- [Cold email for freelance developers: template and rules](https://clientpilot.dev/blog/cold-email-freelance-developer): Example email, two follow-ups, Gmail and Yahoo sender requirements, CAN-SPAM, UK PECR, GDPR and national rules
- [LinkedIn outreach for freelance developers: a 3-step plan](https://clientpilot.dev/blog/linkedin-outreach-freelance-developer): Profile basics, connection note vs InMail vs message, LinkedIn's own invitation limits and automation rules, three example messages
- [Freelance follow-up emails: when, how often, templates](https://clientpilot.dev/blog/freelance-follow-up-email): Timing by situation, what each follow-up should add, four templates incl. a breakup email, a tracking sheet, CAN-SPAM, PECR, GDPR and Gmail/Yahoo notes
- [Freelance developer contract: the clauses that protect you](https://clientpilot.dev/blog/freelance-developer-contract-clauses): Scope and exclusions, change requests, deposits and payment terms, acceptance, IP assignment on full payment under US copyright law, reuse license for your own code, open source, confidentiality, GDPR Article 28 processor terms, warranty, liability cap, termination, handover, and New York City's and New York State's written-contract rules
- [Freelance project proposal: structure and template](https://clientpilot.dev/blog/freelance-project-proposal-template): Structure, length, scope and out-of-scope wording, price options, expiry date, and a copy-paste template for a web development job
- [Upwork proposals for developers: Connects and cover letter](https://clientpilot.dev/blog/upwork-proposal-developer): What the client sees first, how Connects and boosted proposals work, cover letter and screening questions, a short dev example, and why moving off-platform early breaks the Terms of Service
- [Client won't pay? How to chase a late freelance invoice](https://clientpilot.dev/blog/freelance-invoice-late-payment): What to put on the invoice, a reminder schedule with three templates, pausing work and handling client accounts, and the late-payment rules in the EU (Directive 2011/7/EU), the Netherlands, the UK and New York City
- [Freelance developer case study: a structure that wins clients](https://clientpilot.dev/blog/freelance-developer-case-study): What buyers need to see, a template with a made-up example, showing results under an NDA, getting the client's OK and a quote, then publishing on your own site, cross-posting to Dev.to with a canonical URL, and Upwork portfolio and LinkedIn Featured/Projects rules
- [How Toptal, Arc.dev and Lemon.io screen freelance developers](https://clientpilot.dev/blog/freelance-developer-vetting-toptal-arc-lemon): Each screening step as the platforms describe it (Toptal's five steps and pass rates, Arc's communication test and domain interview, Lemon.io's AI or human call, quiz, recruiter call and live technical interview), how to prepare for each, a side-by-side table and a what-to-have-ready checklist
- [Freelance testimonials and referrals: how to ask, and the rules](https://clientpilot.dev/blog/freelance-developer-testimonials-referrals): When to ask, three prompts that get a specific testimonial, request templates for a testimonial, a LinkedIn recommendation and a referral, using testimonials honestly, referral fees and disclosure, and the rules (FTC reviews and testimonials rule, FTC Endorsement Guides, UK DMCC Act 2024, EU Omnibus Directive, GDPR consent)
